newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end firmer on weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end firmer on weaker yen.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended firmer on Thursday in sluggish and narrow-range trade, reflecting the yen's weaker tone against the dollar, traders said.
The newly listed November contract ended flat at 1,357 yen.
Other contracts ranged from five to six yen per gram higher. Benchmark August was six yen firmer at 1,344 yen.
Traders said private investors continued to retreat to the sidelines amid a lack of fresh incentives. They said the main activity was trade houses' spread-trade in line with the currency market.

Palladium futures ended higher, lifted by trade house buying. "After recent sharp falls, some buying interest was detected. But price bounce is likely to stall as the fundamental tone of Japan's palladium market remains bearish," one trader said.
Benchmark palladium August was seven yen firmer at 424 yen.
Silver futures ended mixed while platinum futures were firmer. Benchmark August silver ended 1.2 yen per 10 grams higher at 176.9 yen.
Benchmark August platinum finished six yen per gram firmer at 1,365 yen.
